questions.text: Which operator is used for input in C++?
questions.explanation: The extraction operator `>>` is used with `std::cin` for input.

questions.text: What is the default access specifier for class members?
questions.explanation: In C++, class members are private by default, whereas struct members are public.

questions.text: What is a virtual function used for?
questions.explanation: Virtual functions allow the derived class's implementation to be called even through a base class pointer.

questions.text: Which of these is not an STL container?
questions.explanation: A pointer is a built-in type, not an STL container.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a destructor?
options: To clean up resources when an object is destroyed
questions.explanation: Destructors are called automatically when an object goes out of scope or is deleted.

questions.text: Which keyword is used for generic programming in C++?
questions.explanation: The `template` keyword is used for creating generic classes and functions.

questions.explanation: Multiple inheritance is a feature where a class can inherit from more than one parent class.

questions.text: What is the result of `10 / 4` in C++?
questions.explanation: Integer division in C++ truncates the decimal part.

questions.text: Explain the difference between a `struct` and a `class` in C++.
questions.explanation: The only technical difference is the default access level: `struct` members are public by default, while `class` members are private by default.
A virtual function assigned `= 0`. It makes the class abstract, meaning it cannot be instantiated and derived classes must override it.
RAII is a pattern where resource management is tied to object lifetime. Resources are acquired in the constructor and automatically released in the destructor when the object goes out of scope.

questions.text: What are smart pointers and why should you use them?
questions.explanation: Smart pointers (`unique_ptr`, `shared_ptr`) automate memory management. They ensure memory is freed when it's no longer needed, preventing memory leaks and dangling pointers.

questions.text: What is the Diamond Problem in C++ inheritance and how is it solved?
questions.explanation: It occurs in multiple inheritance when a class inherits from two classes that both inherit from the same base class. It's solved using `virtual` inheritance.
